messages:
sara: Hey @support — incoming escalation from customer acct-789. They see intermittent 400s on /v1/embeddings and recurring tail latency spikes. Customer says they pinned model alias `open-embed` but errors say "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 512" occasionally. Also a lot of long tails when traffic bursts.

mike: Which model variant are they actually calling? Can you paste a raw request example and headers (x-routing-hint, x-tenant-id)?

sara: Customer claim: model alias = open-embed, SDK v1.4.2, requests look like:
```json
{
  "model": "open-embed",
  "input": ["some short text"],
  "client_expect_dim": 1536
}
```
Headers include `x-tenant-id: acct-789`, `x-routing-hint: region:us-west`. They also attached a small repro: send 100 small texts then 1 huge doc.

carla: That 400 implies server-side route was to a 512-dim variant at times. Could be fallback to `open-embed-512` (quantized or legacy) when capacity tight. Did we roll any model canaries?

deploy-bot: canary rollout: open-embed-1536 -> 10% at 2026-03-09T01:23:45Z.

mike: That lines up — canary could be splitting traffic between variants. But fallback should preserve embed dim. Another angle: batching mixing payloads with different model variants leading to weird error on response mapping. Also check batcher coalescing: if batcher coalesces requests for different model variants or dims, response mapping might mismatch.

jonas: Customer describes tail behaviour as "ghost waiters": many small requests coalesced quickly, then a large request arrives and occupies most of a batch slot; small ones wait for flush timeout ~10ms and then flush together forming a huge batch causing long tail. If the large request routes to a different model variant, that could produce the dimension mismatch for some of the coalesced results when responses get misattributed.

sara: Repro steps they provided:
1) Configure client to call `open-embed` pinned.
2) Send 100 requests of ~20 tokens at t=0 (burst).
3) At t=10ms send 1 request of ~2000 tokens.
Result: 20-30s tail on many of the small requests + occasional 400s with dimension mismatch.

infra-bot: logs pulled for request window 2026-03-10T12:00:00Z->12:05:00Z for tenant acct-789, request_id=abc123: found 3 related calls. Routing trace:
- call A: routed to /models/open-embed-1536, status 200
- call B: routed to /models/open-embed-512, status 400 (dimension mismatch)
- call C: routed to /models/open-embed-1536, status 200
Batcher trace shows these were coalesced on same slot id=slot-47 and batch formed with mixed variant routing hints.

mike: Actionable hypotheses:
- routing canary created mixed-variant routing under same alias -> batcher sometimes coalesces across variants (bug).
- batch slotting logic doesn't prevent coalescing of incompatible requests (dim mismatch).
- large requests can starve small ones due to max_batch_size + flush timeout interplay causing tail spikes.

carla: Immediate mitigations we can suggest to customer:
- set `max_batch_size` lower (e.g., 32) and `flush_timeout_ms` to 5ms in their client config to reduce large-batch tails (temp).
- add explicit `x-routing-hint: variant=open-embed-1536` to force consistent variant for testing.

sara: I've asked the customer to try: reduce `max_batch_size` to 32 and send the same repro. Also requested their SDK logs and `x-routing-hint` header values. They responded saying they're willing to test.

jonas: Internal action items for infra/runtime:
1) Enable batcher debug logging for tenant acct-789 for 1 hour: emit `batch-formation` events containing slot_id, request_ids, declared dims, routing_hints.
2) Add assert to prevent coalescing requests with incompatible declared dims (reject with 409 instead of mixing).
3) Audit alias->variant routing logic so fallback/rollout doesn't create mixed-dim served under one alias.
4) Monitor metric `batch_tail_95p` and `coalesced_dim_mismatch_occurrences`.

mike: Also ensure rate limiter doesn't inadvertently delay small requests while large requests hold GPU execution slot. Maybe prioritize small payloads when queue depth > threshold.

infra-bot: toggled batcher debug logging for tenant acct-789 (ttl 1h).

sara: Customer will run the reduced max_batch_size test in ~30 mins. I'll post results here. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

mike: If the repro reproduces, we'll need a quick patch (reject mixed-dim coalescing) and a rollback of the canary rollout until resolved.

carla: Noted. I'll draft the quick patch PR and add a feature flag.

sara: Updating ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/789 — marking as P1 and noting next steps.
